data.title: Compare a soft-body drop against a rigid baseline
data.summary: A 0.3 m rounded cube dropped 0.5 m onto a passive plane. An LLM-assisted recipe with a concrete practice case, visual procedure and review gates.

facts.text: Soft-body settings cover goals, edges, collision and solver behavior.

prerequisites: An authorized Blender / MuJoCo environment and a recorded tool version. Blender-specific references here are pinned to the 4.5 manual; check differences in your installed version.
Practice inputs: A 0.3 m rounded cube dropped 0.5 m onto a passive plane.

Permission to use the source assets and a writable derived-output location. Use a disposable project copy for edits. An MCP connection is optional; reviewed scripts or manual tool actions can follow the same procedure.
steps: Inspect the existing project, asset registry and target runtime for an equivalent soft body drop workflow. Reuse the closest source and preserve its original files.

Give Claude Code, Codex or another authorized coding assistant this practice brief: A 0.3 m rounded cube dropped 0.5 m onto a passive plane. Ask for a small plan and parameter/script diff; verify names and APIs against the installed tool version before applying it.
Preserve a rigid baseline and configure a separate soft-body candidate
Set goal/edge behavior deliberately and record the solver settings
Compare deformation, penetration and recovery over the same frame range

Save the derived candidate separately, record software versions and source/output identities, then perform the acceptance checks. Keep unresolved quality, performance and rights questions in the receipt.
data.output: A versioned compare a soft-body drop against a rigid baseline candidate, the input/parameter table, source identity and a review receipt with the checks below.
validation: The soft candidate does not pass through the plane
The comparison identifies volume loss or unrecovered deformation
Record actual observations separately from expected results; missing tests remain unrun.
limitations: A Blender soft body is not automatically a calibrated finite-element model.
Sintra-authored proposal, not an executed Blender/engine/solver test. The diagram illustrates the procedure and is not a render or execution receipt.
Cloud chat cannot directly control a local 3D app without an appropriate authorized bridge. Tool access, model availability, paid services and rendering resources must be checked separately.
tips: Keep mesh density fixed while testing stiffness settings.
Let the LLM draft and explain bounded changes; use deterministic software to measure geometry, calculate trajectories and validate files.

data.prompt: Help me compare a soft-body drop against a rigid baseline in [existing authorized project]. First find an equivalent asset/workflow and inspect the installed tool version. Practice brief: A 0.3 m rounded cube dropped 0.5 m onto a passive plane. Propose the smallest parameter or script diff and explain each tool action. Follow the linked procedure, preserve original assets and stop on missing inputs or unsupported APIs. Check: The soft candidate does not pass through the plane; The comparison identifies volume loss or unrecovered deformation. Return actual observations, source/output identities and blockers. Do not call expected results completed tests or publish private source paths.
